messages:
Samir: Drafting a short SOP for handling high churn in preemptible GPU pools — PTAL and add gaps.
Marta: +1, please call out metrics to watch.
Samir: Will do. Thinking: eviction-rate, queue-time, active-batch-size, dropped-requests-per-minute.
Jing: Also include 'rebalance' and 'instance rebalance events' from cloud provider. Those often precede spikes.
Samir: Good point. I'll add a detection rule: if eviction-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m, trigger mitigation.
Kevin: For mitigation steps — prefer moving critical loads to reserved pool, not just draining. Draining causes KV cache loss.
Ava: Agreed. Suggest flow: (1) route new requests to reserved; (2) mark affected nodes unschedulable; (3) gracefully terminate long-running inferences.
Samir: Draft mitigation snippet below for k8s: 
```
# mark node unschedulable
kubectl cordon <node>
# evict non-critical pods
kubectl delete pod -l app!=critical --force --grace-period=30 -n inference
```
Marta: 30s grace might be too aggressive for streaming requests — make it 60-90s by default.
Jing: Add a step to snapshot KV cache for pinned sessions when available (we have a cache-export endpoint).
Samir: Noted. Add cache snapshot step and fallback: if snapshot fails, fallback to soft-evict (stop accepting new sessions).
InfraBot: Alert created: #infra-eviction-high when eviction-rate > 0.5% (rule id: evict-high-203).
Kevin: Escalation path: on alert, pager to oncall infra -> if not acked in 5m escalate to infra lead -> if >30m and customer impact, involve SRE oncall.
Ava: Can we auto-apply cheaper mitigation first? e.g., temporarily shift 10-20% traffic to lower-latency reserved instances.
Samir: Yes, we can auto-route using our smart routing policy. Add a policy template: 
```
policy: {
  name: preemptible-churn-smooth,
  when: eviction_rate > 0.005 for 5m,
  actions: [route: {fraction:0.2, target:reserved}, scale: {reserved:+2}]
}
```
Marta: Include cost estimate table in runbook: expected delta = reserved_cost * hours_routed - saved_spot_failures. High level only.
Jing: Also document rollback: how to revert routing and scale when eviction-rate drops below threshold for 10m.
Samir: Add observability checklist: 
- Dashboard: eviction-rate, avg token latency, batch size, infra-p95 latency
- Logs: eviction events, kube-eviction logs, instance lifecycle messages
- Traces: sample failing requests for content-specific regressions

Kevin: Add runbook step: if cache miss rate > 15% after mitigation, run full KV warmup job across reserved pool (script: /ops/warmup-kv.sh).
Ava: Note about mixed pools: annotate pods with "prefer:reserved" for critical models, let autoscaler prefer reserved when counts low.
Samir: I'll add annotation examples. Also adding a brief cost-control section: cap reserved burst to X GPUs per region and timebox for 2 hours.
Marta: Make sure runbook includes contact list and matrix: who to call for infra, SRE, product impact, and customer ops.
Jing: Small item: include region constraint caveat for APAC — some GPU types not available for reserved; fallback to cross-region routing is complex — document manual steps.
Samir: Good catch. Will include cross-region action list and legal check for data residency.
InfraBot: Runbook draft uploaded: https://docs.internal/runbooks/preemptible-churn-sop-v1 (permission: infra-team).
Kevin: Quick ops note: don't rely solely on provider preemption notices — they can be delayed. Use real-time eviction metrics as primary signal.
Ava: We should add a short drill: simulate 20% node loss and validate routing, cache warmup, and customer-facing latency for 30m.
Samir: Will schedule drill in next ops week. Thanks everyone, will push updated draft after lunch. :thumbsup:
Marta: Thanks — lgtm for a first pass.
Jing: happy to review the final runbook.
Samir: Closing thread; will post final JSON link when done.
